F1.quote: Preserving the Ancient Text for Generation Next
F1.claim: the center's motto: preserving the ancient text for the next generation
F1.lineage: what it is: a center that digitally preserves Greek New Testament manuscripts

F2.locus: history panel (the text a reader opens from the home page), ¶ on CSNTM s1
F2.quote: In 2002, Daniel B. Wallace founds the Center for the Study of New Testament Manuscripts (CSNTM) to digitize all surviving Greek manuscripts of the New Testament.
F2.claim: Daniel B. Wallace founded the center in 2002 to digitize all surviving Greek manuscripts of the New Testament

F3.quote: The microfilm images are helpful, but many times they are unclear. For this reason, CSNTM has been producing high-resolution photographs of these documents.
F3.claim: the center produces high-resolution photographs because the microfilm images of the manuscripts are often unclear
F3.lineage: the method: high-resolution photographs where the microfilms are unclear

F4.quote: Since 2002, the team has visited hundreds of institutions in more than 50 countries, digitally preserving their manuscripts.
F4.claim: since 2002 the team has visited hundreds of institutions in more than 50 countries

F5.quote: They have also discovered almost 60 previously unknown manuscripts that can now be found in the official catalog.
F5.claim: the team has discovered almost 60 previously unknown manuscripts now in the official catalogue

F6.quote: Images are available online on the Digital Manuscript Collection website. Scholars visit the website to study manuscript images as they edit the text that stands behind English translations of the New Testament.
F6.claim: the images are online in the Digital Manuscript Collection, where scholars study them as they edit the text behind English translations
F6.lineage: access: the Digital Manuscript Collection and its terms

F7.quote: Through this work, CSNTM helps ensure that readers of the New Testament today hold in their hands the most accurate text possible.
F7.claim: the center states that its work helps ensure readers hold the most accurate text possible
F7.lineage: purpose: the accuracy of the New Testament text

F8.locus: blog post 'Meet the 2026-27 CSNTM Interns!' (25 August 2026), standfirst
F8.quote: At CSNTM, we are dedicated to ensuring that the New Testament you read most accurately reflects the original words of the apostles and early witnesses of Jesus Christ.
F8.claim: the center is dedicated to ensuring the New Testament read today reflects the original words of the apostles and early witnesses of Jesus Christ
F8.lineage: purpose: the accuracy of the New Testament text

F9.locus: blog post 'What CSNTM Identified in the Schøyen Dead Sea Scroll Collection' (24 September 2026)
F9.quote: New findings from our Oslo expedition using multispectral imaging to examine the authenticity of 31 fragments
F9.claim: the center used multispectral imaging in Oslo to examine the authenticity of 31 fragments of the Schøyen Dead Sea Scroll collection
F9.lineage: imaging: multispectral, and work beyond the New Testament

F10.locus: history panel, ¶ on P45, P46, P47 s2–4
F10.quote: P45 and P46 are rather significant because they indicate that already in the third century and at least in some locations, some New Testament writings were compiled into one book.
F10.claim: P45 and P46 show that by the third century, in some places, New Testament writings were compiled into one book
F10.lineage: the Chester Beatty papyri: P45, P46, P47

F11.locus: history panel, ¶ on P45, P46, P47 s5–7

F11.claim: P47 is one of the oldest manuscripts of Revelation, ten leaves, reading 666 at Rev 13:18; the center photographed P45–P47 and produced a facsimile with the holding institutions and Hendrickson
